papers.title: The tensor triangular geometry of valuation domains
papers.abstract: We study the tensor triangular geometry of derived categories of valuation domains, obtaining complete ring-theoretic characterizations of their main structural properties. In particular, although valuation domains are almost always non-noetherian, their derived categories always satisfy the local-to-global principle and hence the detection property. We establish precise criteria for homological detection, stratification, and homological stratification, revealing a clear hierarchy among these properties. Notably, we obtain examples of derived categories of commutative rings that are homologically stratified and satisfy the local-to-global principle, but are not stratified. We also determine when the category of modules over a valuation domain has Gabriel dimension, and use this to provide a negative answer to a question of Balchin, G\'omez and Stevenson. Overall, valuation domains provide a rich class of non-noetherian rings whose derived categories can be understood in considerable depth.

papers.title: Higher zeroes in pointed infinity-categories
papers.abstract: We construct an endofunctor on (small) simplicial sets which freely adjoins a zero object to a (small) infinity-category, as the co-cone construction freely adjoins a terminal object. We then prove that this endofunctor induces a left adjoint to the inclusion of the infinity-category of (small) pointed infinity-categories and morphisms that preserve zero objects into the infinity-category of (small) infinity-categories. This adjunction, in turn, leads to the definition of a coherent choice of nullhomotopies on a pointed infinity-category. A coherent choice of nullhomotopies is a non-canonical, coherent choice of "higher zeroes" on a pointed infinity-category, mirroring the obvious definition of higher zeroes on the differential graded nerve of a differential graded category of chain complexes over an additive category. We then show that coherent choices of nullhomotopies give an alternate characterization of fiber sequences in pointed infinity-categories, generalizing the 1-categorical definition of kernels in terms of morphisms that compose to zero.

papers.title: $K$-theory of finite monoid sets
papers.abstract: In this paper we classify the algebraic K-theory of sets equipped with an action by a finite abelian monoid. The main tool developed for this purpose is an Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem, which gives a decomposition of monoid sets analogous to the decomposition given by the Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem for G-sets.

papers.title: Localisations of rings of weak global dimension at most one
papers.abstract: We characterise the commutative rings of weak global dimension at most one whose derived categories can be stratified by the Balmer-Favi support theory. For such rings, this yields a bijective correspondence between the class of localising subcategories of the derived category, and the subsets of the Zariski spectrum. For a large class of rings of weak global dimension at most one including all valuation domains, this occurs if and only if the ring is locally strongly discrete, if and only if the Telescope conjecture holds, and if and only if the module category has Gabriel dimension. However, we also give an example of a valuation domain where all these conditions fail, and yet the residue fields generate its derived category and we can classify all the localising subcategories of $D(R)$. Additionally, in the same example, we show that the Balchin-Stevenson smashing support cannot stratify $D(R)$ either.

papers.title: Combination Theorems and the Farrell--Jones Conjecture for Graph Products of Pairs
papers.abstract:
We study the Farrell--Jones conjecture for graph products of pairs and for fundamental groups of polyhedral products. We introduce a pair-deletion decomposition and a local notion of FJ-admissibility, and prove a vertexwise combination theorem for graph products of pairs. The criterion applies, in particular, to ordinary graph products, free-factor pairs, suitable normal pairs, and classes controlled by acylindrical Bass--Serre actions.
  For polyhedral products, we combine these results with their description by relative graph products and graph products of pairs. We also obtain bounds and exact computations for amenable category, together with applications to simplicial volume and Borel rigidity of closed aspherical polyhedral-product manifolds.

papers.title: Smooth and Topological Nonorientable Four-Genera of Low-Crossing Knots
papers.abstract: We compare linking-form bounds with the smooth and locally flat nonorientable 4-genera of low-crossing knots. For every prime knot with at most 13 crossings whose Witt-level linking-form bound is at least 2, this bound equals both genera. We also exhibit 41 prime knots with 12 or 13 crossings that bound locally flat M\"obius bands but no smooth ones, and whose smooth nonorientable 4-genus is 2. Our methods combine linking forms, Heegaard Floer correction terms and definite-lattice obstructions with explicit band constructions. They determine 3,300 of the 3,525 values left unknown in KnotInfo on 2 November 2026; the remaining 225 knots have range $[1,2]$. We obtain new lower bounds of 2 for 2,102 knots with 14 crossings and correct previously reported values for three knots with 11 crossings.

papers.title: The $p$-local topologoical period-index problem in dimensions $2p+2$ and below
papers.abstract: For any odd prime number $p$, we solve the topological period-index problem for a $p$-primary element of the Brauer group of a CW-complex of dimension not greater than $2p+2$.

papers.title: Toward Quillen stratification for the odd primary Steenrod algebra
papers.abstract: Fix an odd prime $p$ and let $A$ be the mod $p$ Steenrod algebra. There is a normal sub-Hopf algebra $D$ of $A$, and we show that the cohomology of $A$ is $F$-isomorphic to the subalgebra of the cohomology of $D$ which is invariant under the $A$-action. We also show that the sub-Hopf algebras of $A$ with bounded profile function detect nilpotence in cohomology.

papers.title: Algebraic $\mathbb{A}^{1}$-invariance of K-theory for affinoid Tate adic spaces of good reduction
papers.abstract: We establish homotopy invariance for connective continuous K-theory of affinoid Tate adic spaces of good reduction with respect to the algebraic affine line, distinct from the adic affine line as analytic stacks. We approach this through an investigation of boundedness of t-structures on nuclear module categories, to which end we also study ultrasolid modules, a variant of solid modules, and their properties.

papers.title: $L^2$-Betti numbers of Dehn fillings
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of the $L^2$-Betti numbers of group-theoretic Dehn fillings. For a broad class of virtually special groups $G$, we prove that the $L^2$-Betti numbers of sufficiently deep Dehn fillings $\overline{G}$ are equal to those of $G$. As applications, we verify the Singer Conjecture for certain Einstein manifolds, establish a virtual fibering criterion for $\overline{G}$, obtain bounds on deficiency of $\overline{G}$, and provide new examples of hyperbolic groups with exotic subgroups that arise as Dehn fillings of any cusped arithmetic hyperbolic manifold of dimension at least four.

papers.title: $P=W$ via $\mathcal{H}_2$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_2$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial Hamiltonian vector fields on the symplectic plane. Let $X$ be the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles of fixed relatively prime rank and degree, or more generally the moduli space of stable parabolic Higgs bundles of arbitrary rank and degree for a generic stability condition. Let $H^*(X)$ be the cohomology with rational coefficients. Using the operations of cup-product by tautological classes and Hecke correspondences we construct an action of $\mathcal{H}_2$ on $H^*(X)[x,y]$, where $x$ and $y$ are formal variables. We show that the perverse filtration on $H^*(X)$ coincides with the filtration canonically associated to $\mathfrak{sl}_2\subset \mathcal{H}_2$ and deduce the $P=W$ conjecture of de Cataldo-Hausel-Migliorini.

papers.title: A Bubble Compactification of KSBA Moduli Space of Surfaces of General Type
papers.abstract:
We construct a bubble-tree enhancement of the KSBA moduli space of surfaces of general type using index-one-cover Deligne--Mumford stacks. The construction is inspired by bubbling phenomena for K\"ahler--Einstein metrics. Non-klt semi-log-canonical singularities are replaced by admissible simple-normal-crossing configurations: the cusp and degenerate-cusp components are rational, while the simple-elliptic case also contains elliptic ruled components. A key feature is that the construction avoids lci covers.
  We construct the moduli stack of polarized bubble-tree index-one-cover Deligne-Mumford stacks. The stack is in general not separated, and we construct its underlying separated algebraic space. We also construct the moduli stack of bubble-tree index-one-cover Deligne-Mumford stacks with labeled sections that record algebraic bubbling centers and compare it with the pointed metric bubble tree. The labeled sections determine a numerical class whose stability proves the separatedness of the moduli stack.
  We establish a perfect obstruction theory and a virtual fundamental class on the bubble-tree moduli stacks. This provides a novel and geometric pathway to prove the existence of a virtual fundamental class on the original KSBA moduli space, thus offering a new approach to a conjecture of Donaldson. We expect that parts of the construction extend to higher dimensions.

papers.title: A certified lower bound for the essential minimum of the Zhang-Zagier height
papers.abstract: Let h be the absolute logarithmic Weil height. We prove that the essential minimum of the Zhang-Zagier height h(a)+h(1-a) is at least 0.2497815: for every d > 0, only finitely many algebraic numbers a satisfy h(a)+h(1-a) < 0.2497815 - d. The previous best lower bound was 0.24874 (Flammang, 2018). The proof combines Smyth's auxiliary-function method, with the polynomials of Doche and of Flammang, and the condition that the discriminant of the minimal polynomial is a nonzero integer, in the potential-theoretic form used by Smith and by Orloski, Talebizadeh Sardari and Smith for the trace problem. The infimum of the resulting auxiliary function is bounded below rigorously by monotone interval bounds and adaptive bisection, from a stored certificate. The statement concerns the essential minimum and is weaker in nature than the pointwise bounds of Doche and Flammang.

papers.title: A note on prismatic sites for p-quasisyntomic rings
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a fixed prime number and let $R$ be a $p$-quasisyntomic ring. We provide conditions for objects in the absolute prismatic site $R_\Prism$ to cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and to admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$. More precisely, we introduce in $R_\Prism$ the so-called transversal objects, so that the coproduct of any object in $R_\Prism$ with a transversal object exists in $R_\Prism$. As an immediate generalization, we introduce the so-called relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid covers of $R$, whose prismatic cohomology (of $\delta$-pairs, in the sense of Antieau-Krause-Nikolaus) produces objects in $R_\Prism$ that cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$.

papers.title: A Note on Topological Hochschild Homology Relative to $\Sphere_{W(k)}[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n]$
papers.abstract: We explain the relation between the relative topological Hochschild homology $\THH(R/\Sphere_{W(k)}[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$ and the Nygaard-completed Frobenius-twisted relative prismatic cohomology $\widehat{\Prism}^{(1)}_{R/W(k)[x_0,\ldots,x_n]^\wedge}$, where $W(k)[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n]\rightarrow R$ is relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid. As an application, for $R=\Z_p[x]/(px)$, we compute $\pi_*\THH(R)^\wedge_p$ by descent along $\THH(R)^\wedge_p\rightarrow \THH(R/\Sphere_p[z,x])$, where $R$ is regarded as an $\Einfty$-$\Sphere_p[z,x]$-algebra via $\Sphere_p[z,x]\xrightarrow{z\mapsto p,x\mapsto x}\Z_p[x]/(px)$.

papers.title: A Relative Telescope-Type Conjecture: Support and Generation in Half-Bounded Derived Categories
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative noetherian ring. We ask whether complexes with finitely generated cohomology and a fixed support can be generated by relatively compact objects, using coproducts which exist in the half-bounded derived category. We prove that $\mathbf D^+_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R)=\operatorname{Loc}_{\mathrm{ex}}(\mathbf D^b_{\mathrm{fg},W}(R))$ whenever $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec} R$ is specialization closed and has finite dimension. The same equality holds for every specialization-closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec} B$ when $B$ is a finite-type algebra over a noetherian domain $A$ of finite character and either $A$ or $B$ is regular. These equalities classify the thick Hom-submodules closed under existing coproducts. We also prove the corresponding bounded-above statement from the support results of Matsui--Takahashi. For an arbitrary noetherian ring, the bounded-below generation conjecture reduces to torsion complexes over quotient domains, with their support unchanged. Finally, over a regular noetherian domain of infinite dimension, we give a bounded-below object which is generated by bounded objects with the same support but has no bounded-below representative by finitely generated modules. The comparison functor from the bounded-below derived category of finite modules is therefore neither full nor essentially surjective.

papers.title: A Torelli-type theorem for hyperk\"{a}hler quotients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the moduli space of algebraic asymptotic hyperk\"{a}hler structures on hyperk\"{a}hler quotients arising from a quaternionic vector space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We consider the period map on this moduli space, and prove a Torelli-type theorem (i.e., the bijectivity of the period map) under mild assumptions including the surjectivity of the Kirwan map. This work provides an algebro-geometric generalization of the Torelli-type theorem for ALE gravitational instantons by Kronheimer (1989). In particular, this theorem applies to toric hyperk\"ahler varieties and Nakajima quiver varieties.

papers.title: Admissible extremal rays and the anticanonical minimal model program
papers.abstract: We develop an anticanonical minimal model program for projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial klt pairs $(X,\Delta)$ such that $-(K_{X}+\Delta)$ is pseudoeffective. We first prove the cone and contraction theorems for potentially klt triples and establish the existence of flips for such triples. Using these results, we introduce the notion of admissible extremal rays and show that $(K_{X}+\Delta)$-positive admissible extremal rays are precisely the rays that are to be contracted by $-(K_{X}+\Delta)$-MMP. The elementary MMP steps associated to such admissible rays preserve klt singularities. For potentially klt pairs $(X,\Delta)$ with $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $\Delta$, we prove that every $(K_{X}+\Delta)$-positive extremal ray is admissible and obtain a cone theorem for the $(K_{X}+\Delta)$-positive part of the Mori cone. Assuming termination of the anticanonical minimal model program, we establish a dichotomy: potentially klt pairs admit anticanonical minimal models, whereas non-potentially klt pairs admit non-admissible models.

papers.title: Algebraic ellipticity of double covers of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$
papers.abstract: We show that every smooth complex double cover of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$ branched along a smooth divisor of tridegree $(2,2,2)$ is algebraically Gromov elliptic. These irrational Fano threefolds form Mori--Mukai family 3-1 and have anticanonical genus seven and Picard rank three. Their three coordinate projections define degree-four del Pezzo fibrations. Each threefold also admits a dominant rational map of degree two from $\mathbf P^3$.

papers.title: Algebraicity, Hodge Gradings, and the Geometry of Period Images
papers.abstract: We prove the algebraicity of period images in arithmetic quotients without using o-minimality. The proof uses infinitesimal neighborhoods and formal algebraization to recover the images and the maps from their algebraic sources. Hodge positivity and an algebraic ampleness criterion yield the Griffiths polarization and quasi-projectivity. For lifted images, we construct Stein neighborhoods and holomorphic matrix realizations of the Hodge filtration. On closed horizontal subspaces, we bound canonical Bergman density below by the Hodge volume form. We compare the Bergman and Griffiths--Schmid metrics near one-parameter boundaries with nontrivial unipotent monodromy and nondegenerate graded period maps, and in all directions near general one- and two-node quintic threefolds. A period surface arising from abelian threefolds shows that the upper metric comparison fails in general.

papers.title: Alperin weight bijections and dimensions of simple modules
papers.abstract: We propose a new refinement of the (blockwise) Alperin weight conjecture taking dimensions of simple modules (or degrees of irreducible Brauer characters) into consideration. This is similar to Giannelli's refinement of the (Alperin--)McKay conjecture. We prove this new refinement for blocks with a cyclic or Klein four defect group, for inertial blocks (which include the Brou\'{e}--Puig nilpotent blocks), and for $p$-blocks of $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: An infinitesimal deformation of the post-Lie and post-Hopf algebra correspondence
papers.abstract: We describe infinitesimal deformations of post-Lie algebras and post-Hopf algebras and prove that the universal enveloping algebra and primitive elements adjunction is compatible with the infinitesimal structure. In characteristic zero, this restricts to an equivalence for connected cocommutative infinitesimal post-Hopf algebras, extending the Cartier--Milnor--Moore theorem. We parametrize all infinitesimal post-Lie structures on $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ and exhibit a second-order obstruction. From a geometric point of view, infinitesimal post-Lie algebras emerge from flat connections with covariantly constant torsion and an additional compatible symmetric $(1,2)$-tensor. This leads to explicit examples of infinitesimal post-Lie structures based on Heisenberg Lie algebras. On the Hopf side, we classify infinitesimal structures above the trivial action, prove rigidity for group algebras, and describe the structures on Sweedler's Hopf algebra. The subadjacent construction induces a Hopf algebra deformation with fixed coproduct. Finally, we prove that the quadratic operad of infinitesimal post-Lie algebras is Koszul, using a filtered distributive law between the operads of Lie algebras and bi-magmas.

papers.title: Anticanonical divisor with good asymptotic base loci
papers.abstract: We characterize varieties of Fano type in terms of potentially log canonical pairs and birational Zariski decompositions. We also prove the existence of anticanonical minimal models of a potentially lc pair $(X,\Delta)$ under the assumptions that no potentially log canonical centers are contained in the augmented base locus of $-(K_X+\Delta)$ and that $-(K_X+\Delta)$ is a big $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor admitting a birational Zariski decomposition with NQC positive part. This can be considered as an anticanonical analogue of the results by Birkar--Hu.

papers.title: Approaching the Continuous from the Discrete: an Infinite Tensor Product Construction
papers.abstract:
Increasingly in recent years, probabilistic computation has been investigated through the lenses of categorical algebra, especially via string diagrammatic calculi. Whereas categories of discrete and Gaussian probabilistic processes have been thoroughly studied, with various axiomatisation results, more expressive classes of continuous probability are less understood, because of the intrinsic difficulty of describing infinite behaviour by algebraic means.
  In this work, we establish a universal construction that adjoins infinite tensor products, allowing continuous probability to be investigated from discrete settings. Our main result applies this construction to $\mathsf{FinStoch}$, the category of finite sets and stochastic matrices, obtaining a category of locally constant Markov kernels, where the objects are finite sets plus the Cantor space $2^{\mathbb{N}}$. Any probability measure on the reals can be reasoned about in this category. Furthermore, we show how to lift axiomatisation results through the infinite tensor product construction. This way we obtain an axiomatic presentation of continuous probability over countable powers of $2=\lbrace 0,1\rbrace$.

papers.title: Base change between canonical basis and path basis
papers.abstract: Almost 30 years ago Littelmann conjectured that there is a unitriangular base change between the dual canonical basis and the path vector basis for all symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras. In this paper we give a positive answer to the conjecture for the case of classical Lie algebras and type $G_2$, when the path model is given by standard Young tableaux.

papers.title: Bayesian Filters via the Stochastic Category
papers.abstract: We extend the categorical treatment of Bayesian filters to models with feedback, whose transitions and observations may depend on the past observations. We work in the stochastic category, whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are Markov kernels, which we refer to as stochastic morphisms. We systematically parameterize stochastic morphisms by a measurable space, and develop the calculus of conditioning in a notation intuitively compatible with classical probability theory, requiring neither string diagrams nor densities. A stochastic morphism into a product space is regarded as a parameterized family of joint laws, and its conditional law is again a stochastic morphism, so that the rules of conditioning become equalities of stochastic morphisms. We define the Bayesian inverse with respect to a parameterized prior and prove Bayesian coherence. A model with feedback is then a model whose parameter space grows with the observations, and we derive the Bayesian filter, prediction and smoothing for such models, with standard Borel hidden states and countably generated observation spaces. The affine Gaussian stochastic morphisms parameterized by a measurable space form a family strictly larger than the Markov category $\mathbf{Gauss}$, closed under composition and Bayesian inversion, in which we obtain the Kalman filter and the Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother with feedback.

papers.title: Between Markov and restriction. Two more monads on categories for relations
papers.abstract: The study of categories abstracting the structural properties of relations has been extensively developed over the years, resulting in a rich and diverse body of work. In a previous paper we offered a survey providing a modern presentation of these ``categories for relations'' as instances of gs-monoidal categories, showing how they arise as Kleisli categories of suitable symmetric monoidal monads. The end result was a taxonomy that organised numerous related concepts in the literature, including in particular Markov and restriction categories. This paper further enriches the taxonomy: it proposes two categories that are once more instances of gs-monoidal categories, yet more abstract than Markov and restriction categories. They are characterised by an axiomatic notion of mass and domain of an arrow, the latter one of the key ingredients of restriction categories, which generalises the domain of partial functions. The paper then introduces mass and domain preserving monads, proving that the associated Kleisli categories in fact preserve the corresponding equations and that these monads arise naturally for the categories of semiring-weighted relations.

papers.title: Binomial Artin-Schelter Regular Algebras and Twisted Monoid Algebras
papers.abstract: We study four-dimensional binomial Artin-Schelter regular algebras and their connection with twisted monoid algebras. Starting with $23$ examples up to permutation of generators, we investigate the associated monoids of I-type and the structure of their groups of fractions. We determine the corresponding finite permutation groups and compute the second group cohomology $H^2(G(M),k^\times)$. These computations allow us to construct explicit families of four-dimensional Koszul Artin-Schelter regular algebras through cocycle twists. We illustrate this construction for some of these algebras.

papers.title: Boundary determination from the anisotropic elastic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
papers.abstract: We show that the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the elastic wave equation determines the density and the anisotropic stiffness tensor on the boundary for generic density and stiffness tensor fields. The proof builds on an interplay between microlocal analysis and algebraic geometry. Microlocal analysis yields a construction of special solutions, valid for many real principal type systems, that concentrate near a boundary point. Generic conditions ensure that this construction holds and allow for extraction of information about stiffness tensor and density at the boundary. We also describe the generic sets through algebraic conditions.

papers.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties in Characteristic Zero
papers.abstract: We construct a canonical projectivization of every smooth proper algebraic variety $X$ in characteristic zero. Once a principalization procedure is fixed, the construction gives a finite sequence of blowups in smooth centers with smooth projective endpoint, natural under semilinear isomorphisms and preserving the quasi-projective core, the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective open subsets. At each stage we select finitely many ideals near the generic points of the image in $X$ of the boundary of a maximal quasi-projective open. Principalizing their product strictly lowers the dimension of that image. The selection is defined intrinsically, without a polarization or a chosen projective modification; a Hilbert scheme argument proves its finiteness. Naturality embeds the automorphism group in that of a smooth projective variety of the same dimension. We then extend the construction to smooth proper integral algebraic spaces, obtaining canonical projectivizations of all compact connected Moishezon manifolds.

papers.title: Cartan determinants for almost laura, quasi-laura, semilinear clannish and piecewise Bäckström algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the Cartan determinant conjecture for corners of finite global dimension in almost laura, quasi-laura and (m)-quasi-laura Artin algebras, finite-dimensional piecewise Bäckström algebras, and semilinear clannish Artin algebras of finite dimension over their defining division ring.

papers.title: Categorical foundations of discrete dynamical systems
papers.abstract: We develop categorical foundations of discrete dynamical systems, aimed at understanding how the structure of the system affects its dynamics. We introduce the notion of cycle sets to analyze attractors of a system, and use this to generalize multiple decomposition theorems of Kadelka, Veliz-Cuba, Murrugarra, and the last two authors from Boolean networks to arbitrary discrete dynamical systems.

papers.title: Cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-Homology from Bruhat Boundary Matrices of Split Semisimple Flag Varieties
papers.abstract: We determine the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-chain complex of full and partial flag varieties of split semisimple simply connected groups over a perfect field of characteristic different from 2. With compatible integral normal orientations and reindexing by opposite Bruhat cells, the differential in each degree at least two is represented by the motivic Hopf map $\eta$ times one half of the signed cellular boundary matrix of the corresponding real flag manifold. Consequently, the Smith data of the resulting integer complex give all positive-degree cellular homology sheaves in terms of Milnor--Witt $K$-theory and the kernels and cokernels of integer multiples of $\eta$. We obtain a uniform computation of the second cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of $SL_n/B$ for $n\geq3$, together with complete calculations for $SL_3/B$ and the full flags of types $F_4$ and $G_2$.

papers.title: Co-Decompositions and FO Model Checking
papers.abstract:
Tree decompositions describe large graphs as gluings of smaller component parts. Here we study their categorical duals, tree co-decompositions, which construct large graphs via fibered products of small constituent parts. Co-decompositions are compressed representations of graphs or relational structures: the decomposed object can be exponentially larger than the space required to specify the co-decomposition.
  Our main contribution is an algorithmic meta-theorem for first order logic: given only a co-decomposition of a $\sigma$-structure $G$ with $b$ bags, each of size at most $w$ and an FO sentence $\phi$, there is an algorithm which, without ever constructing or inspecting $G$, operates on the co-decomposition and determines whether $G \models \phi$ in time $f_\sigma(w,|\varphi|)\cdot b$. We pair this algorithm with structural results on tree co-width, including its relationship to tree-width and a separation from twin-width. Furthermore, we characterize bounded path co-width using a graph grammar. In contrast to our logical meta-theorem, we prove that $(s,t)$-Path becomes NP-hard on co-decomposition inputs. These results demonstrate how categorical constructions can enable efficient computation on exponentially compressed structures.

papers.title: Cohomology of vector bundles on the moduli space of parabolic connections on $\mathbb{P}^1$ minus $5$ points
papers.abstract: We study the moduli space of parabolic connections of rank two on the complex projective line $\mathbb{P}^1$ minus five points with fixed spectral data. We prove a cohomological vanishing theorem for tensor products of four natural vector bundles on the moduli stack of $\nu$-${\mathfrak sl}_2$-parabolic connections. We also compute the cohomology of the structure sheaf and give an explicit geometric description of a compactification of this moduli space, using $\epsilon$-connections and the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}^2 \times (\mathbb{P}^2)^{\vee}$. As an application, we construct a universal family of twisted $D$-modules whose fibers satisfy an orthogonality property over a dense open subset. These results are motivated by Arinkin's approach to the tamely ramified geometric Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Compatible gradings on dg models and cluster equivalence
papers.abstract: Let $\La_1$ and $\La_2$ be finite-dimensional $\ta_2$-finite complex algebras of global dimension at most two. We prove that, if they are cluster equivalent, then they admit $\bbZ$-gradings for which the bounded derived categories of graded modules are triangle equivalent. The equivalence is not required to commute with the internal grading shifts. The proof uses common multigraded dg models, relative gradings on two-term silting objects, and covering quotients. We also consider tilting lifts of cluster-tilting objects with endomorphism algebras of global dimension at most two. In acyclic cluster type, the existence of such a lift for every cluster-tilting object implies piecewise heredity. We construct a counterexample without this assumption using a surface algebra associated with a one-holed torus.

papers.title: Complete Diagrammatic Axiomatisations of Relative Entropy
papers.abstract: Relative entropy is a fundamental class of distances between probability distributions, with widespread applications in probability theory, statistics, and machine learning. In this work, we study relative entropy from a categorical perspective, viewing it as a quantitative enrichment of categories of stochastic matrices. We consider two natural monoidal structures on stochastic matrices, given by the Kronecker product and the direct sum. Our main results are complete axiomatisations of Kullback-Leibler divergence and, more generally, of R\'enyi divergences of arbitrary order, for each such structure. Our axiomatic theories are formulated within the framework of quantitative monoidal algebra, using a graphical language of string diagrams enriched with quantitative equations.

papers.title: Computer-assisted bounds 0.556921 <= p_c <= 0.6463 for site percolation on the square lattice
papers.abstract: Let p_c be the critical probability of Bernoulli site percolation on Z^2. We prove 0.556921 <= p_c <= 0.6463. The previous best rigorous bounds known to us are p_c >= 0.5567 (Ashton, 2026, extending van den Berg and Ermakov, 1996) and p_c <= 0.666894 (Wierman and Oberly, 2024). The lower bound uses the growth-process comparison of van den Berg and Ermakov with the exact posterior on the exploration tree. We reduce this posterior to a scalar interval recursion and explore the tree generation by generation, with a prescribed order among siblings. This passes the value 0.556788... that the same scalar computation gives when the order is not used, and the value 0.556788090 reported by Ashton as the limit of his relaxation. The upper bound uses the substitution method of Wierman, in two stages with 4x4 regions, from the line graph of Z^2 (site threshold 1/2) to Z^2. Both bounds are certified by short pure-Python programs in exact rational and integer arithmetic.

papers.title: Conic Multiview Varieties
papers.abstract: We present an algebraic study of projections of conics in space onto multiple images of pinhole cameras. We study the Zariski closures of the projection images, which we call conic multiview varieties. Extending previous work for point and line multiview varieties, we use back-projected cones to describe these varieties. For two views, we determine the defining ideals of conic multiview varieties and describe their singular loci. For any number of views, we characterize when the simplest possible set-theoretic description is achieved based on the geometry of the camera centers. Finally, we investigate the complexity of the associated triangulation problem and conjecture the Euclidean distance degree for the conic multiview variety for two cameras.

papers.title: Conjecture B for $X_{10}$ and its genus-two mirror
papers.abstract: We prove Conjecture B of Akhtar--Coates--Corti--Heuberger--Kasprzyk--Oneto--Petracci--Prince--Tveiten unconditionally for the normalized family of maximally mutable Laurent polynomials with prescribed $T$-binomial edge coefficients associated with the degree-10 orbifold del Pezzo hypersurface $X_{10}\subset\mathbb{P}(1,2,3,5)$. An explicit $S$-extended quantum-period calculation determines the affine mirror map $\lambda=a-346$ and proves that the regularized quantum period equals the classical period as a formal power series throughout the family.

papers.title: Contextful Arrows via Wreath Products
papers.abstract:
We introduce contextads and the Ctx construction, unifying various structures and constructions in category theory dealing with context and contextful arrows---comonads and their Kleisli construction, actegories and their Para construction, adequate triples and their Span construction. Contextads are defined in terms of Lack--Street wreaths, suitably categorified for pseudomonads in a tricategory of spans in a 2-category with display maps. The associated wreath product provides the Ctx construction, and by its universal property we conclude trifunctoriality. This abstract approach lets us work up to structure, and thus swiftly prove that, under very mild assumptions, a contextad equipped colaxly with a 2-algebraic structure produces a similarly structured double category of contextful arrows.
  We also explore the role contextads might play qua dependently graded comonads in organizing contextful computation in functional programming. We show that many side-effects monads can be dually captured by dependently graded comonads, and gesture towards a general result on the `transposability' of parametric right adjoint monads to dependently graded comonads.

papers.title: D-equivalence conjecture for hyperk\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type
papers.abstract: We show that birationally equivalent hyperk\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type are derived equivalent, confirming the D-equivalence conjecture in this case. Combined with recent results of other authors, this settles the conjecture for all known deformation types of hyperk\"ahler varieties. The kernel is built from an equivariant Fourier-Mukai kernel on the sum-zero loci of powers of an abelian surface. We deform it along diagonal twistor paths, using the hyperholomorphic endomorphism algebra. Comparing wall hyperplanes gives a common twisted derived category for two adjacent birational models, and a finite sequence of wall crossings then gives the equivalence.

papers.title: Decompositions of homomorphisms of abelian $p$-groups with $p^2$-bounded target
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime. We classify homomorphisms $H:V_1\to V_2$ between abelian $p$-groups that are direct sums of cyclic groups, under the assumption $p^2V_2=0$. We prove that every such homomorphism is isomorphic to a direct sum of finite indecomposable representations and that this decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and reordering of the summands.

papers.title: Derived Equivalences for Terminal Threefold Flops via Local Index-One Covering Models
papers.abstract: Inspired by the quadratic involutions of Corti-Pukhlikov-Reid and Gavin Brown's description of hypersurface flips via toric GIT, we apply similar symmetries to local covering models of terminal threefold flops. We recover the derived equivalence of their canonical stacks by pullback and pushforward along the fibre product over the canonical stack of the contraction target, revisiting the local picture in Kawamata's work.

papers.title: Derived Ringel duality through finite subquotients of modular category $\mathcal O$
papers.abstract: We study derived Ringel duality for modular category $\mathcal O$ on downward-closed, quasi-bounded supports. We reconstruct global tilting objects and their morphisms from compatible images in finite highest-weight Serre subquotients, and realize the complete Ringel algebra as an inverse limit of finite-dimensional algebras. The duality identifies the bounded homotopy category of finitely generated projectives over the associated locally unital algebra with the bounded derived category of the Ringel dual category. We characterize tiltings recovered, together with their outgoing morphisms, by a single finite subquotient, and give a sharp criterion for equivalence under Frobenius restriction. For $SL_2$, we compute tilting endomorphism algebras and their quotient maps, and obtain sharp recovery bounds for finite tilting families.

papers.title: Discrete homotopy groups of cubical sets
papers.abstract: We extend the notion of discrete homotopy groups of graphs to arbitrary cubical sets, and show that the discrete homotopy groups of quasisymmetric cubical sets are naturally isomorphic to the homotopy groups of their geometric realizations. Here, quasisymmetric cubical sets are cubical sets equipped with coordinate permutation symmetries that are compatible with faces and degeneracies, but not necessarily with connections. We give a purely combinatorial construction of the left adjoint of the forgetful functor from the category of quasisymmetric cubical sets to the category of cubical sets, and prove that the unit of this adjunction is a natural weak equivalence. As a consequence, we obtain a purely combinatorial description of the homotopy groups of the geometric realizations of arbitrary cubical sets. As an application, we establish the discrete Hurewicz map from the discrete homotopy groups of a cubical set to the homology groups, and prove a Hurewicz theorem with respect to the discrete Hurewicz map whenever the cubical set is quasisymmetric. Applied to the 1-nerve of a directed graph, it also yields a Hurewicz theorem relating the homotopy groups of Li, Wu, Yau, and Zhang to singular cubical homology.

papers.title: Dwork Motives, Monodromy and Potential Automorphy
papers.abstract:
In this paper we study certain families of motives, which arise as direct summands of the cohomology of the Dwork family. We computationally find examples of interesting families with the following three properties. Firstly, their geometric monodromy group is Zariski dense in $\operatorname{SL}_n$. Secondly, they realise many different unipotent operators as the monodromy operator at $t = \infty$. Thirdly, all their Hodge numbers are $\leq 1$.
  This has consequences for Galois representations. Namely, if a nilpotent operator $N$ appears as the monodromy at $t = \infty$ in one of our families, we can construct potentially automorphic representations with $\ell$-adic monodromy given by $N$ at a fixed prime $p$. As another application, we obtain a new proof of some cases of the recent local-global compatibility theorem of Matsumoto.

papers.title: Effective results in representation theory of reductive groups over local fields
papers.abstract: We prove effective versions of several classical results in representation theory of reductive groups over non-Archimedean local fields of arbitrary characteristic. More specifically, we deal with the support of matrix coefficients of cuspidal representations and the recursions satisfied by matrix coefficients of representations of finite length. We provide effective generation results for irreducible representations. Finally, we study the effective smoothness of characters on the set of regular semi-simple elements.

papers.title: Energy Solutions and Harnack Estimates for Nonlocal Drift–Diffusion
papers.abstract: We consider nonlocal drift–diffusion equations of order $2s\in[1,2)$ with bounded divergence-free drift. The symmetric measurable jump kernel satisfies local coercivity, a global upper form bound, and a scale-invariant bound on the intensity of long jumps. The transport form is bounded and skew-symmetric on $H^{1/2}\times H^{1/2}$. In the fractional energy space, distributional and variational solutions coincide and satisfy nonlinear testing identities. Viscous approximations converge strongly in $C_tL^2_x\cap L^2_tH^s_x$ to the unique solution of the Cauchy problem. For sources bounded in the cylinder, supersolutions nonnegative there satisfy a weak Harnack inequality involving the time integral of the negative exterior tail. Under this source bound, locally bounded solutions whose exterior tail belongs to $L^q$ in time for some $q>1$ are locally Hölder continuous. This also gives Hölder continuity at positive times for homogeneous global solutions with $L^2$ data. Under upper jumping smoothness, control of the positive tail on an earlier time interval yields the full parabolic Harnack inequality for solutions nonnegative on the full spatial slab. A kernel supported on alternating dyadic annuli satisfies all the kernel assumptions. The local estimates depend on the drift through $R^{2s-1}\|b\|_\infty$.

papers.title: Enumerative geometry of conics and double covers on projective complete intersections
papers.abstract: We compare genus zero degree two Gromov--Witten invariants with the number of embedded conics on general projective complete intersections whose conic space has expected dimension zero. Their difference comes from double covers of lines. We compute this contribution as an integral of Chern classes over the Fano scheme of lines, using an explicit obstruction bundle on the compactified space of double covers.

papers.title: Extended Contact Algebras: Algebraic analysis and duality theory
papers.abstract: The ternary extended contact relation studied in (Ivanova, 2020) is a more expressive counterpart of the standard, well-known binary contact relation. Boolean algebras expanded with this relation are called Extended Contact Algebras (ECAs). In this work, we take an algebraic perspective on ECAs, interpreting the ternary relation as a form of entailment. To this end, we introduce the class of Pseudo-Inference Algebras, i.e., Boolean algebras equipped with a monotone ternary operator, additive in its first two coordinates, and satisfying additional equations that capture the logical character of the extended contact. We show that the subclass of relational Pseudo-Inference Algebras corresponds precisely to ECAs and generates the variety of strict PSI-Algebras, which is a discriminator variety. Furthermore, building on the duality developed in (Celani, 2009), we introduce descriptive PSI-frames and establish three interrelated dualities that differ in their morphisms while sharing the same class of topological objects. The resulting framework provides a relational semantics for PSI-Algebras, connecting spatial and logical notions within a categorical and topological setting.

papers.title: Fat base schemes and unexpected hypersurfaces of type $(d+k,d)$
papers.abstract:
We study hypersurfaces of degree $d+k$ containing a prescribed zero-dimensional fat point scheme $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ and having multiplicity at least $d$ along a general codimension-two linear subspace. We associate with this interpolation problem a vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1$ whose splitting type determines the dimensions of all linear systems of type $(d+k,d)$.
  For a fat point of multiplicity $m$, we determine the exact number of conditions detected by this bundle and introduce the corresponding effective length. This leads to an excess formula separating the contributions of the splitting type, the part of the fat structure invisible to degree-$k$ fibrewise sections, and the Hilbert-function defect of the fixed scheme.
  We also prove a truncation theorem showing that multiplicities larger than $k$ contribute only a uniform twist of the bundle and, geometrically, fixed hyperplane components. Finally, we exhibit explicit planar and three-dimensional examples showing that genuinely unexpected phenomena persist for nonreduced fixed base schemes, including geometrically irreducible unexpected hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Flag Varieties of General Quiver Representations: Characteristic Classes and Semi-Invariants
papers.abstract: We study flags of subrepresentations of a general representation of a finite quiver. For each representation, its flag scheme is the zero scheme of a section of a quotient bundle on a product of partial flag varieties. We obtain the generic dimension and cycle class and equivariant localization formulas for Euler characteristics and parabolic Schubert coefficients. We further express these coefficients as finite signed sums of semi-invariant dimensions for auxiliary star quivers with inward and outward flag arms. In the acyclic one-step case, this is compatible with the result of Derksen--Schofield--Weyman, and the zero-dimensional case recovers their semi-invariant counting theorem. Examples treat matrix pencils and generalized Kronecker quivers.

papers.title: Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex, which can be considered as a derived variant of the module of Frobenius--Witt differentials defined by T. Saito. This new object also can be seen as an arithmetic variant of the notion of cotangent complex. We explain the suitability of these two viewpoints through a series of propositions. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes and the regularity of noetherian local rings, which can be considered as a derived variant of Saito's regularity criterion. This proof relies heavily on computations of Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes in the case of perfectoid rings. We also study the deformation theory of delta structures using Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes.

papers.title: Functoriality and the theta correspondence
papers.abstract: We study the functoriality of the local theta correspondence for classical $p$-adic groups. This is realized via the adaptation of the Adams conjecture to ABV-packets. We provide evidence for the conjecture, especially in the case of general linear groups.

papers.title: Fundamental groups, coregularity, and low dimensional klt Calabi-Yau pairs
papers.abstract: In this article, we study how the absolute coregularity of a projective log pair reflects on its fundamental group. More precisely, we conjecture that for a projective klt log pair $(X,D)$ of absolute coregularity $c$ (and arbitrary dimension) the fundamental group $\pi_1^{\rm reg}(X,D)$ admits a normal abelian subgroup of finite index and rank at most $2c$. We prove this conjecture in the cases $0 \leq c \leq 3$, building on the almost abelianity of the fundamental groups of klt Calabi-Yau pairs of dimension $\leq 3$. In the cases $c \in \{0,1,2\}$ and fixed dimension, we can furthermore bound the index of a solvable normal subgroup. In dimension three, we are able to prove almost abelianity of the fundamental group of the regular locus for projective klt Calabi-Yau pairs.

papers.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
papers.abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

papers.title: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings
papers.abstract: We study the least pole order of a rational function whose nonzero evaluations scale a prescribed code to a Euclidean LCD code. A residue-one differential yields an obstruction for odd-dimensional one-point AG codes in characteristic two: for $C=C_L(D,aQ)$ with $0\le a<n$ and odd dimension, the threshold is at least $n+2g-a-1$. The obstruction uses alternating Gram matrices and does not require the scaled code to be self-orthogonal. For the dimension-three codes $C_L(D,(r+1)Q)$ on Hermitian curves over $\F_{r^2}$, $r=2^e\ge4$, we obtain \[ n+2g-r-2\le\tau_D(C;Q)\le n+2g-3. \] Consequently the leading genus contribution is asymptotically sharp even in dimension three. On the elliptic curve $y^2+y=x^3$ over $\F_4$, we prove the exact dimension-three threshold $6$ by an explicit multiplier. For repetition codes on the Hermitian family, the threshold equals the general interpolation bound $n+2g-1$. The upper bounds use information sets and hold for $q>3k$, and for $q>2k$ in characteristic two.

papers.title: Geometry of Spaces of Subrings
papers.abstract: Motivated by examples such as the local rings of projective integral schemes and the Zariski-Riemann space of a field, we develop a geometry for continuously indexed families of subrings of a commutative ring $R$. The indexing spaces are Stone spaces, and continuity is taken with respect to the Zariski topology on the space of subrings. To each such family we associate a subsheaf of the constant sheaf with value $R$ whose stalks are the indexed subrings. This gives a patch ringed space. Its global sections are locally constant $R$-valued functions whose value at each point belongs to the corresponding subring. The ring of global sections, with this representation, is the associated patch algebra. Our main result establishes an algebra-geometry correspondence between these continuously indexed families of subrings and patch ringed spaces that can be expressed as a category equivalence, with each of the two categories dually equivalent to the category of patch algebras. Thus the indexing space, its sheaf, and the indexed subrings can be recovered functorially from the associated patch algebra, which serves as a coordinate ring for this geometry. We describe kernels and factorizations of patch algebra morphisms in geometric terms and characterize their injectivity and surjectivity. We include applications to Pierce duality and Bhatt-Scholze $w$-localizations of integral separated quasi-compact schemes.

papers.title: Gepner stability conditions on hypersurface categories
papers.abstract: We construct numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the category of graded matrix factorizations of every smooth complex projective hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$. These conditions are of Gepner type $(\tau,2/d)$, where $\tau$ is the grading shift autoequivalence. By Orlov's theorem, this gives stability conditions of Gepner type on all Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and on Kuznetsov components of all Fano hypersurfaces. These conditions satisfy a mass-Hom bound and the support property on the full numerical Grothendieck group. Semistable objects of fixed numerical class and phase admit proper good moduli spaces.

papers.title: Global vector fields and the automorphism group of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
papers.abstract: For a connected regular semisimple Hessenberg variety other than the full flag variety, we prove that the identity component of its automorphism group is an algebraic torus. The argument uses equivariant local coordinates and weight-homogeneous coefficient functions of vector fields.

papers.title: Hecke Relations from Self-Duality
papers.abstract: Hecke operators can be used to relate characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges, but it has remained a mystery how to interpret these relations physically. We offer a simple explanation in terms of self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds. Self-dual orbifolds also give more general identities beyond the familiar Harvey-Wu construction, which we illustrate through examples.

papers.title: Hierarchical filtrations of vector bundles and birational geometry
papers.abstract: We study chains of locally free subsheaves of equal rank whose successive quotients are nonzero divisorial torsion sheaves. Fixing the determinant of the initial term defines a normalized hierarchical depth. An ample intersection argument proves finiteness on every smooth projective variety. On an algebraically closed smooth projective curve, the depth equals the degree of the determinant difference precisely when that difference is effective; otherwise, no normalized filtration exists. For birational morphisms of smooth projective surfaces, reflexive pushforward contracts exactly those steps whose determinant divisors are entirely exceptional. This yields a comparison of filtration lengths without a commutativity assumption. Explicit examples show that pullback can strictly increase depth and compute a depth of twenty on a two-point blowup. Finally, we distinguish preservation of evaluation codes for genuinely descended bundles from removal of zero coordinates caused by exceptional fixed components. The coding statements use specified compatible fiber bases or the block Hamming metric.

papers.title: Highest weight vectors, shifted topological recursion and quantum curves
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of topological recursion by considering Airy structures whose partition functions are highest weight vectors of particular $\mathcal{W}$-algebra representations. Such highest weight vectors arise as partition functions of Airy structures only under certain conditions on the representations. In the spectral curve formulation of topological recursion, we show that this generalization amounts to adding specific terms to the correlators $ \omega_{g,1}$, which leads to a ``shifted topological recursion'' formula. We then prove that the wave-functions constructed from this shifted version of topological recursion are WKB solutions of families of quantizations of the spectral curve with $ \hbar$-dependent terms. In the reverse direction, starting from an $\hbar$-connection, we find that it is of topological type if the exact same conditions that we found for the Airy structures are satisfied. When this happens, the resulting shifted loop equations can be solved by the shifted topological recursion obtained earlier.

papers.title: Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras: a Kauffman diagram perspective
papers.abstract: We describe Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras by explicit minimal-resolution coordinates and multilinear operations on Kauffman diagrams. For each doubled-line basic algebra, a finite four-term bimodule complex is verified by a signed-shuffle comparison and an augmented contracting homotopy. We compute cocycles and coboundaries and recover the known cup product and Gerstenhaber bracket in explicit representatives. Over $\mathbb C$, at nonzero root-of-unity loop parameters, we construct a tower-compatible derivation and the marked-circle two-cocycle. Their classes are nonzero on every nonsemisimple block; their cup products therefore represent all positive classes over the centre. Relative full twists give a compact expression for the derivation. Worked planar diagrams distinguish the cup product from insertion and strict cochain equalities from equalities of classes. A finite-lattice section interprets the marked-circle operation as loop-weight response, derives its planar Potts normalization, and exhibits a six-vertex realization. It also shows why passing to a deformable spin representation may annihilate the class with different coefficients. No thermodynamic conclusion is claimed, and the even-strand zero-parameter family remains separate.

papers.title: Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra
papers.abstract: Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Intuitionistic Compression and Optimal Verification Trees
papers.abstract: In strict finitistic generation semantics, a formula is assertible at a generation if some stage in its verification tree forces it. We ask when assertibility agrees with intuitionistic truth on the poset of generations. The leaves of the verification trees, ordered by generation extension, form an intuitionistic Kripke model that preserves truth at every leaf, even without atomic prevalence. For a finite bundle, compression to the generations is exact if and only if each fiber of leaves has a greatest intuitionistic theory and the map selecting these theories has the back property. Compression remains exact under every restriction of the generation poset if and only if atomic prevalence holds. Conversely, consider coherent tree representations of a finite Kripke model whose atomic valuation reflects its order. Among representations with atomic prevalence, the minimum numbers of leaves and nodes over $u$ are $h(u)$ and $\delta_C+\sum_{x\preceq u}h(x)$, where $h(x)$ counts saturated paths from minimal worlds to $x$, and $\delta_C$ is $1$ if the comparability component of $u$ has no least element and $0$ otherwise. Saturated-path trees attain both minima simultaneously. Among representations attaining the node minimum at every world, the common root labels in components without a least element determine the representation up to isomorphism over the outer frame. Allowing rooted posets in place of trees can reduce the number of nodes exponentially.

papers.title: Isolated symplectic singularities admitting symplectic resolutions
papers.abstract: We give a proof that an isolated algebraic symplectic singularity of dimension $2n\ge 4$ admitting a projective symplectic resolution is analytically isomorphic to the minimal nilpotent orbit closure in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ at the origin.

papers.title: K-theory of Gieseker variety and type A cyclotomic Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We give an algebraic description of the equivariant K-theory of Gieseker varieties. Our main result identifies the equivariant K-theory of the Gieseker space with the Jucys--Murphy center of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra, over the equivariant K-theory of a point. The construction is inspired by the proof of the Hikita--Nakajima conjecture for Gieseker spaces given by the first and third authors. We discuss consequences for the center of cyclotomic Hecke algebras and for specializations to q=1 and to roots of unity. In particular, we relate K-theory of affine type A quiver varieties with the centers of the corresponding blocks of specialized cyclotomic Hecke algebras. This last result strengthens the correspondences obtained by the second author in earlier work.

papers.title: K3 Categories and Mukai Homomorphisms for Debarre-Voisin Varieties
papers.abstract: Let $M=X_6^\sigma$ be a smooth Debarre-Voisin hyperk\"ahler fourfold and $X=X_3^\sigma$ the associated smooth hyperplane section of $\operatorname{Gr}(3,10)$. Using the incidence correspondence between $X$ and $M$, we construct a family $\mathcal E$ of objects in the Kuznetsov component $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$. We write $v$ for the common Mukai vector of its fibers. We prove that the associated Mukai homomorphism \[ \Theta_{\mathcal E}|_{v^\perp}\colon v^\perp\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(M,\mathbb Z) \] is an integral Hodge isometry and explicitly determine the inverse image of the Pl\"ucker polarization. For a very general point of the trivector divisor corresponding to discriminant $24$, we also construct an integral Hodge isometry between the full Mukai lattices of $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$ and the associated twisted K3 surface.

papers.title: Kernel Dimension of the Z/2 Connection Laplacian on a Finite Simple Graph (A Formalisation in Lean 4 / Mathlib v4.11.0)
papers.abstract: We present a Lean 4/Mathlib v4.11.0 formalization of the kernel-dimension theory of the $\mathbb{Z}/2$ connection Laplacian on finite simple graphs equipped with designated wrap edges. Each edge carries either the identity or the coordinate-swap matrix. A Hadamard–Kronecker change of basis decomposes the resulting rank-two connection Laplacian into the ordinary and signed graph Laplacians. An analogous splitting holds for the scalar Laplacian of the associated two-sheeted cover. A connected component is balanced precisely when its covering preimage has two connected components, equivalently when its sign holonomy is trivial along every closed walk. Consequently, the nullity of the signed Laplacian equals the number of balanced connected components, while the nullity of the full connection Laplacian equals the number of connected components plus the number of balanced components. For the flat connection, the nullity is twice the number of connected components. We also formalize exact characteristic polynomials and eigenvalue multisets, including multiplicities, for explicit ordinary and one-wrap signed cycle matrices for $n \geq 3$. Transfer to general connection-graph encodings remains conditional on specified matrix-reindexing identities. The contribution is a machine-checked formalization, exposition, and documented verification of results rooted in classical signed-graph spectral theory, rather than a claim of priority for those identities. The accompanying repository preserves proof artifacts, computational cross-checks, historical verification evidence, and documented corrections.

papers.title: Least-Atom Extremizers for Resampling Noise
papers.abstract: A single least-mass atom determines the extremal behavior of resampling noise on a finite probability space. A fixed-moment comparison gives the sharp generalized Samorodnitsky inequality for every \(1<q<2\) through one scalar curve, and identifies all nonconstant scalar extremizers. The same principle determines every \(L^p\)-to-\(L^q\) resampling norm for \(1<p<q<\infty\), resolving a conjecture of Cao, Fan, Han, Qiu, and Wang. The sharp hypercontractive parameter increases strictly with the least atom. The uniform-binary phase diagram is explicit, and product equality cases are classified for every nonuniform reference law and for the uniform binary law.

papers.title: Local resolution of the second log-Fitting ideal
papers.abstract: Logarithmic Fitting ideals encode the complexity of the corresponding morphisms in a natural and intrinsic way, and their principalisation offers a new perspective on problems such as the resolution of cotangent sheaves and the monomialisation of morphisms. In this paper, we give a local resolution theorem for log-rank adapted morphisms: after finite sequences of smooth local blow-ups, the first two log-Fitting ideals \mathcal{F}\_{n--1}(\sigma) and \mathcal{F}\_{n--2}(\sigma) become principal monomial ideals.

papers.title: Log-concavity in the Newton basis and support of rank-two scattering coefficients
papers.abstract: We prove that polynomials with nonnegative, interval-supported log-concave Newton coefficients are closed under multiplication and, for integer Newton coefficients, under \(D(m)\mapsto\binom{D(m)}k\) for integers \(k\ge0\). Coordinatewise Newton multiplication preserves two-variable Schur positivity. We also determine the exact positive Newton support of symmetric rank-two cluster scattering coefficients.

papers.title: Mapping class group actions on the cohomology of configuration spaces of surfaces
papers.abstract: Let X be a closed oriented surface of genus at least 2 and P a finite subset of X. We bound the action of the mapping class group of (X,P) on the rational cohomology groups of the ordered configuration spaces F_n(X-P) of X-P. In particular, we show that, when #P < 2, the diagonal action of the mapping class group on the direct sum of the H^n(F_n(X-P)) is faithful, and determine its kernel when #P > 1.

papers.title: Min-plus Bruhat decomposition
papers.abstract: We study min-plus Bruhat cells $B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$, where $B_{trop}^{(n)}$ denotes the set of all upper-triangular matrices over $\RR \cup \{\infty\}$, and $p$ is a permutation. It is proved that $\dim (B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p \odot B_{trop}^{(n)})= \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + l(p)$, where $l(p)$ is the length of $p$ in Coxeter generators. Also we provide an explicit description of the cell $B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR) \odot p_0\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR)$ (up to a subset of dimension less than $n^2$) for the highest in Bruhat order permutation $p_0$. Finally, it is shown that for a tropically non-singular matrix $A$ for at most one permutation $p_A$ it can hold $A\in B_{trop}^{(n)}\odot p_A\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$.

papers.title: Monoidal and symmetrized parametrized topological complexity
papers.abstract: We introduce and study monoidal and symmetrized versions of parametrized topological complexity. First, we develop parametrized analogues of the monoidal topological complexity theories of Iwase--Sakai, Aguilar-Guzm\'an--Gonz\'alez (based on the Fadell--Husseini approach), and Dranishnikov. We investigate the parametrized Iwase--Sakai conjecture and provide sufficient conditions under which it holds. We then introduce symmetrized parametrized topological complexity and combine it with the monoidal perspective to define monoidal symmetrized parametrized topological complexity, showing that the resulting notions agree. Finally, we compute these invariants for Fadell--Neuwirth fibrations.

papers.title: Nested Squares and Distinct-Prime Goldbach Partitions
papers.abstract: The distinct-prime Goldbach conjecture asserts that for every $N\geq 4$ there is $M\in A_N=[1,N-3]$ with $N-M$ and $N+M$ both prime; geometrically, nested squares of side lengths $N$ and $M$ have an L-shaped difference of semiprime area $(N-M)(N+M)$. With $C_N$ and $D_N$ the sets of $M\in A_N$ for which $N-M$, respectively $N+M$, is prime, the conjecture for $2N$ is $C_N\cap D_N\neq\varnothing$. We embed this centered condition in a straddling one: $C_N\cap D_N$ lies in the set $E_N$ of half-differences $(Q-P)/2\in A_N$ of primes $2<P<N<Q<2N$. From Mikawa's theorem on prime pairs with almost all differences we deduce $|A_N\setminus E_N|\ll_D N/(\log N)^D$ for every $D>0$, and with explicit constants we prove $|E_N|>N/760$ for every $N\geq 3275$. Consequently, for all large $N$ and all but $O_D(N/(\log N)^D)$ primes $P<N$, the number $2N-P$ becomes prime after adding the difference $P'-P$ of two primes $P'<N$; Goldbach's partition is the case $P'=P$. In contrast, $|C_N\cap D_N|<(N-3)-\log^2(2N)$ for every $N\geq 34$, and covering all but $\log^2(2N)$ values of $A_N$ for all large $N$ would imply the Cram\'er-type bound $p'-p<2\log^2(2p+2)+2$. The method also shows that $2N$ is a sum of two distinct primes for more than $X/9600$ integers $N\leq X$, for every $X\geq 10^6$. Computations up to $N=10^6$ compare the number of distinct-prime partitions with the Hardy--Littlewood prediction and measure the missing values of $E_N$ forced by prime gaps. The conjecture itself is not proved here.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean Riesz-Frechet Representation
papers.abstract: We derive a Riesz-Frechet representation for bounded linear functionals defined on the p-adic Hilbert spaces introduced by Kalisch [\textit{Ann. of Math. (2), 1947}]. We also notice the surprising difference between the Archimedean case and the non-Archimedean case (exact non-Archimedean version of Riesz-Frechet representation fails).

papers.title: Non-Cartesian Guarded Recursion with Daggers
papers.abstract: Guarded recursion is a framework allowing for a formalisation of streams in classical (as opposed to concurrent, probabilistic, quantum) programming languages. The latter take their semantics in cartesian closed categories. However, some programming paradigms do not take their semantics in a cartesian setting; this is the case for concurrency, reversible and quantum programming for example. In this paper, we focus on reversible programming through its categorical model in dagger categories, which are categories that contain an involutive operator on morphisms. We show how to introduce the framework of guarded recursion into dagger categories with sufficient structure for data types, also called dagger rig categories. First, given an arbitrary category, we build another category shown to be suitable for guarded recursion in multiple ways, via enrichment and fixed point theorems. We then study the interaction between this construction and the structure of dagger rig categories, aiming for reversible programming. Finally, we show that our construction is suitable as a model of higher-order reversible programming languages, such as symmetric pattern matching, to which we add guarded recursion features.

papers.title: Normality of marginal inverse subsemigroups in inverse semigroups
papers.abstract: For each pair of integers $m\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2$, we construct a finite inverse semigroup $S_{m,n}\subseteq M_m(\mathbb{C})$ and explicitly determine its marginal inverse subsemigroup $M_{x^n}(S_{m,n})$ associated with the word $x^n$. We prove that the three conditions $\sim_{x^n}=\equiv_{x^n}$ on $S_{m,n}$, $M_{x^n}(S_{m,n})\trianglelefteq S_{m,n}$, and $m\le n$ are equivalent. As a consequence, we answer Problem 11 of Ara\'ujo, Ara\'ujo and Kinyon in [1]. Moreover, for a word $\omega$ in any inverse semigroup $S$, we prove that $\sim_\omega=\equiv_\omega$ if and only if $M_\omega(S)\trianglelefteq S$ and $\sim_\omega$ is invariant under inversion.

papers.title: On Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers
papers.abstract: We prove Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers for each $m \geq 3$ on the normalized logarithms of Euler characteristics of moduli spaces. Also, we state a log-concavity conjecture on Euler characteristics near slope one for the 3-Kronecker quiver.

papers.title: On Shilov boundaries, Rees valuations and integral extensions
papers.abstract:
We explore an analogy between, on one hand, the notions of integral closure of ideals and Rees valuations in commutative algebra and, on the other hand, the notions of spectral seminorm and Shilov boundary in nonarchimedean geometry. For any Tate ring $\mathcal{A}$ with a Noetherian ring of definition $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ and pseudo-uniformizer $\varpi\in\mathcal{A}_{0}$, we prove that the Shilov boundary for $\mathcal{A}$ naturally coincides with the set of Rees valuation rings of the principal ideal $(\varpi)_{\mathcal{A}_{0}}$ of $\mathcal{A}_{0}$.
  Furthermore, we characterize the Shilov boundary for a wide class of Tate rings by means of minimal open prime ideals in the subring of power-bounded elements. For affinoid algebras, in the sense of Tate, whose underlying rings are integral domains, this recovers a well-known result of Berkovich. Moreover, under some mild assumptions, we prove stability of our characterization of the Shilov boundary under (completed) integral extensions. In particular, for every mixed-characteristic Noetherian domain $R$, we obtain a description of the Shilov boundary for the Tate ring $\widehat{R^{+}}[p^{-1}]$, where $\widehat{R^{+}}$ is the $p$-adic completion of the absolute integral closure of the domain $R$.

papers.title: On silting theory for complete path algebras
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a finite quiver and let $\Lambda$ be the complete path algebra of $Q$ with respect to the arrow ideal. We study the mutation of silting objects in the bounded homotopy category of projective $\Lambda$-modules and characterise in which cases the mutation theories of silting complexes and 2-term silting complexes of $\Lambda$ are determined by those of a finite dimensional quotient $\Lambda/I$. This characterisation is closely related to a characterisation of 2-term silting finite quotient algebras.

papers.title: On the $abc$ conjecture
papers.abstract: Using adelic intersection theory and following the method envisioned by Parshin and Moret-Bailly, we prove a conjecture of Vojta for curves of genus two and a weak form of the $abc$ conjecture

papers.title: On the Brill--Noether Theory of Sheaves on Regular Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Brill--Noether theory of higher rank sheaves on surfaces $X$ with $H^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X) = 0$ and its interactions with the classical Brill--Noether theory of line bundles on curves lying on $X$. Denoting by $\mathrm{Spl}(v)$ the moduli space of simple sheaves on $X$ with Chern character $v = (r,c_1,\mathrm{ch}_2)$, we introduce the Brill--Noether loci $BN^k(v)^\circ \subseteq \mathrm{Spl}(v)$ of \emph{generically $k$-generated} sheaves and show, under assumptions on $c_1$ and $K_X$, certain well-behavedness results. In particular, if $c_1$ is \emph{indecomposable} and $X$ is a K3 surface, we generalize a Brill--Noether theorem for sheaves on K3s due to Yoshioka. This is achieved by employing He's deformation theory of the moduli space of coherent systems and a globalization of the Lazarsfeld--Mukai construction, providing a correspondence between the Brill--Noether theories of generically $r$-generated sheaves on $X$ and that of line bundles on curves $C \in |c_1|$. The same techniques yield upper bounds on the dimension of $\mathcal{W}^{r,\mathrm{bpf}}_d(|c_1|) \setminus \mathcal{W}^{r+1}_d(|c_1|)$ consisting of basepoint-free line bundles in terms of the number of endomorphisms of associated Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, for arbitrary $c_1$. This generalizes a result of Aprodu and Farkas in the context of Green's conjecture beyond K3 surfaces. In the case $r = 1$ of pencils, we obtain smoothness and expected-dimension results under an effectivity condition on $-K_X|_C$ for $C \in |c_1|$. As an application, we prove Green's conjecture for the general curve on a rational surface with a nef and effective anticanonical divisor.

papers.title: On the Haagerup Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Three constructions of vertex operator algebras realizing the Haagerup center were announced independently and almost simultaneously. The relations between these constructions are studied in this paper. The generators are expressed in a common lattice basis for $E_6\oplus A_2$. It is proved that the constructions of Riesen and Huang give isomorphic vertex operator algebras, and that this algebra and the algebra constructed by Jiao have isomorphic fixed point subalgebras under automorphisms of order two. The isomorphisms are given explicitly on generators. The common fixed point subalgebra contains the parafermion vertex operator algebras $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,3)$ and $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,13)$. A general rationality criterion for unitary vertex operator algebras is given in terms of positive linear combinations of conformal vectors and is applied to these constructions. The two vertex operator algebras are simple current extensions of the common fixed point subalgebra and have equivalent module categories as ribbon categories. The equivalence follows from decomposition with respect to a nondegenerate pointed subcategory with four simple objects in the module category of the common fixed point subalgebra. It is also proved that the conformal nets associated with these unitary vertex operator algebras are completely rational.

papers.title: On the Hodge and Tate conjectures for moduli spaces of curves
papers.abstract: We survey recent progress on the cohomology of moduli spaces of stable curves through the lens of the Hodge and Tate conjectures, especially their generalized coniveau forms, which relate Hodge structures and l-adic Galois representations on cohomology to algebraic cycles. We explain how the inductive structure of the boundary stratification verifies these conjectures in a surprisingly wide range of cases, describe the guiding inspiration from arithmetic, and discuss open problems and directions for future research.

papers.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $\rho$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)$ is the $\rho(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $\Pi(\rho)$ under Scholze's functor, and $\Pi(\rho)$ is the representation associated to $\rho$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: On the Orthogonal Projections
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra and $e$ a rigid presentation. We give an explicit formula for the left adjoint to the inclusion $\operatorname{rep}(e^\perp)\hookrightarrow \operatorname{rep}(A)$ and construct a bijection between presentations in $\operatorname{rep}(e^\perp)$ and presentations compatible with $e$. The induced bijection on weights preserves generic $\operatorname{E}$-invariants and canonical decompositions. If $A$ is Jacobian, the reduction algebra is Jacobian for every rigid $e$. We prove mutation formulas for the signed completions and for the dimension vectors of the simple objects of $\operatorname{rep}(e^\perp)$, enabling an algorithm to find the projected quiver with potential when $e$ is extended-reachable.
