Additionally, we introduce a modified projection for quivers with potentials that preserves general presentations. For applications to cluster algebras, we establish a connection to the stabilization functors.

papers.title: On the representability of actions of unital algebras
papers.abstract: Working in the setting of ideally exact categories, we investigate the representability of actions of unital non-associative algebras over a field. We show that, in general, such categories fail to be action representable: for instance, the category of all unital algebras is not even action accessible. We then consider this problem in the context of operadic, action accessible, unit-closed varieties. Using the construction of the external weak actor, we prove that for any algebra $X$ in such a variety $\mathcal{V}$, the canonical map into its external weak actor is an isomorphism if and only if $X$ is unital. Consequently, the ideally exact category $\mathcal{V}_1$ of unital algebras in $\mathcal{V}$ is action representable, and the actor of a unital algebra $X$ is $X$ itself. The action accessibility of $\mathcal{V}$ is not necessary for this conclusion: in characteristic zero, unital Jordan algebras form an action representable category, although the variety of all Jordan algebras is not action accessible. Finally, we prove action representability for the categories of unital Poisson algebras and unital commutative Poisson algebras.

papers.title: Positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cones on compact complex surfaces
papers.abstract: We determine the positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cone of every minimal compact K\"ahler surface of Kodaira dimension $-\infty$. By the Enriques--Kodaira classification, every such surface is either $\mathbb P^2$ or a geometrically ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $E$ is a rank-two holomorphic vector bundle over a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. On $\mathbb P^2$, every K\"ahler class admits a K\"ahler metric of positive scalar curvature, whereas on $\mathbb P(E)$, every K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admits a metric of positive scalar curvature if and only if $g\le1$ or $E$ is slope-semistable. We further prove that if a smooth compact K\"ahler surface admits a birational morphism onto a ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $g\ge2$ and $E$ is slope-unstable, then it contains a K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admitting no positive scalar curvature K\"ahler metric. Finally, for every smooth compact K\"ahler surface $X$ birational to $Y=\mathbb P^2$ or $Y=\mathbb P(E)$, we show that K\"ahler classes admitting positive scalar curvature metrics on $Y$ are exactly the pushforwards of classes admitting such metrics on $X$.

papers.title: Projective symmetries of Chebyshev polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $\varphi_d$ be the monic Chebyshev polynomial defined by $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$. For $d>4$ with $p\nmid d$, let $H_d\le\text{PGL}_2(k)$ be the stabilizer of the zero set of $\varphi_d$. We show that \[ H_d\cong \begin{cases} D_d,&\text{if }2d=p^r+1\;\text{ for some integer }\;r\geq 1,\\ S_3,&\text{if }4d=p^r+1\;\text{ for some integer }\; r\geq 1,\\ C_2,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

papers.title: Pseudo-Einstein Structures on Links of Isolated Singularities
papers.abstract: We study Jack Lee's conjecture that, for a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$, the condition $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{R})$ implies the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. For links of isolated singularities, we construct counterexamples in every odd dimension at least three, with $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_1(M)=0$. For isolated algebraic singularities of log canonical type and complex dimension at least three, we prove that the real Chern class condition is equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartierness of the canonical divisor, log canonicity, and the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. Finally, we construct a Du Bois threefold singularity whose link satisfies the real Chern class condition but admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. The initial versions of the proofs were generated with AI assistance and were subsequently revised and verified by the authors.

papers.title: Pushforwards of lc pairs under morphisms to abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a morphism from a log canonical pair $(X,\Delta)$ to an abelian variety $A$ and $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}m(K_X+\Delta)$ a Cartier divisor on $X$ with $m>1$ a rational number. We prove that $f_*\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ is globally generated after pullback by an isogeny. Our methods involve birational geometry, mixed Hodge modules and singular Hermitian metrics with the minimal extension property. Moreover, we provide simple counterexamples where the above result fails for plt pairs when $m=1$ and where the existence of Chen--Jiang decompositions fails for plt pairs for any $m\ge1$.

papers.title: Quadratic Complexity of Voronoi Diagrams in $\mathbb{R}^3$ for Lines in a Single Ruling of a Regulus
papers.abstract:
We study nearest and farthest Voronoi diagrams of lines in three-dimensional Euclidean space, which partition space according to the closest and farthest input lines, respectively. For arbitrary lines, a gap remains between the known quadratic lower bound and near-cubic upper bounds for the complexity of the nearest diagram. We consider input lines chosen from one of two continuous families of straight lines on a smooth surface defined by a quadratic equation, with one line from each family passing through every point of the surface.
  Under the geometric assumptions stated in the paper, we prove quadratic upper bounds on the total number of vertices, edges, faces, and connected three-dimensional regions in both diagrams. We also construct quadratically many nearest vertices using lines from a single family on one fixed surface, establishing a tight quadratic worst-case bound. The farthest diagram has quadratic total complexity for every input satisfying our assumptions.
  Our proof uses a parametrization that arranges the input lines in a cyclic order and expresses tangency to a sphere by a polynomial equation of degree four. At a Voronoi vertex, the four tangent input lines give four distinct roots. The sign changes between these roots, together with the nearest or farthest condition, force two intervening parameter intervals to contain no other input parameters. Thus, only quadratically many choices of four lines can define a vertex, and each choice yields at most eight isolated candidate centers.

papers.title: Ramified tori and Gelfand--Kirillov dimension of mod $p$ representations
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension of degree $n$ with $p\geq3$, and let $D$ be the non-split quaternion algebra over $K$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional admissible smooth representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(K)$ or $D^\times$ with a central character and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition has Gelfand--Kirillov dimension $n$. As a corollary, every infinite-dimensional admissible Banach representation whose locally analytic vectors have an infinitesimal character has dimension $n$, strengthening Sorgdrager's bound to an equality. An appendix by Yongquan Hu proves that, when $K\ne\mathbb{Q}_p$ and the coefficient field is algebraically closed, the canonical diagram of an admissible supersingular representation satisfying the same Casimir annihilation condition is $(\pi,\pi,\mathrm{id})$, as in the case of local fields of characteristic $p$.

papers.title: Rational points on loxodromic K3 surfaces and complex dynamics
papers.abstract: We establish an analogue of the Hilbert irreducibility theorem for all K3 surfaces over number fields that admit an automorphism of positive entropy. Our method draws ingredients from both algebraic geometry and complex dynamics.

papers.title: Reconstruction of F-cohomological field theories on moduli of compact type
papers.abstract: We prove an analogue of Givental-Teleman reconstruction for F-cohomological field theories on the moduli space of compact type. We apply it to reconstruct the restriction of the extended $r$-spin classes to the extended direction and deduce relations between $\kappa$-classes (both in compact type).

papers.title: Relative cohomology and base-change
papers.abstract: In this note we prove a simple generalization of cohomology and base-change which seems to be missing from standard sources. We illustrate its usefulness by providing an alternative proof of a result of Ishimura on descent of vector bundles along blowups at a smooth center.

papers.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $\Lambda=\pi_1^{alg}(G)$, the Galois group $\Theta=Gal(L/K)$ acting on $\Lambda$, where $L$ is a finite Galois extension of $K$ having no real places, the decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v\subseteq \Theta$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. We also compute $Sha^S(K,G)$ in some cases where $S$ contains archimedean places.

papers.title: Remarks on the Farthing--Muhly--Yeend inverse semigroup of a finitely aligned higher-rank graph
papers.abstract: Given a finitely aligned higher-rank $k$-graph $\Lambda$, Farthing, Muhly and Yeend (Semigroup Forum 2005) constructed an inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$ to provide a groupoid model for the $C^*$-algebra of $\Lambda$. In this paper, we extend some of the existing results related to the semigroup structure of a graph inverse semigroup to the more general setting of the inverse semigroup $S_\Lambda$. We obtain geometric descriptions of the Green's relations on $S_\Lambda$, which effectively generalize the existing characterization of Green's relations on a graph inverse semigroup. We provide a simple and useful description of the Cuntz-Krieger ideal of the Booleanization of $S_\Lambda$ and, based on this, identify a certain $X$-to-join Booleanization of $S_\Lambda$, where the abstract and concrete Cuntz-Krieger relations agree. Besides the natural partial order, $S_\Lambda$ is also ordered by set-inclusion. This helps us to realize $S_\Lambda$ as a semigroup \emph{graded-ordered} by $\mathbb{Z}^k$ and, subsequently, gives rise to a full inverse subsemigroup $S_\Lambda^h$ of $S_\Lambda$, which is graded by $\mathbb{Z}^k$ in the usual sense. We show that the Kumjian-Pask algebra of $\Lambda$ is graded isomorphic to the quotient of the contracted semigroup algebra of $S_\Lambda^h$ by the tight ideal. In the final part of the paper, we show that a $k$-graph morphism $p:\Lambda_1\longrightarrow \Lambda_2$ that is injective and satisfies a certain path lifting property induces, in a natural way, an injective $0$-preserving semigroup homomorphism from $S_{\Lambda_1}$ to $S_{\Lambda_2}$. In view of this, we build a suitable categorical setup to conclude that the isomorphism established between the Kumjian-Pask algebra of $\Lambda$ and the tight ideal quotient of the semigroup algebra of $S_\Lambda^h$ is natural.

papers.title: Seshadri constants of singular loci of line arrangements with at most twelve lines
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathcal L}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the complex projective plane and let $Z={\operatorname{Sing}}({\mathcal L})$. A question of Pokora asks whether the multipoint Seshadri constant of ${\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1)$ at $Z$ is always computed by a line of the arrangement containing the largest number of points of $Z$. We prove that the answer is affirmative for every arrangement of at most twelve lines. The proof uses a B\'ezout-type covering criterion, elementary restrictions on the intersection lattice, and a detailed analysis of the two extremal combinatorial types that can occur for twelve lines. One type is the Hesse arrangement; it is handled using a net of quartics through its twelve double points. The other type would yield a uniquely determined incidence structure on thirteen lines. We show that this incidence structure is not realizable over any field.

papers.title: Skein and cluster algebras of punctured surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the full Fock--Goncharov conjecture for the $\mathcal{A}_{SL_2,\Sigma_{g,p}}$-cluster variety associated with the moduli space of decorated twisted $SL_2$-local systems on triangulable surfaces $\Sigma_{g,p}$ with at least two punctures. Equivalently, we show that the tagged skein algebra $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$, identified with the middle cluster algebra $\mathrm{mid}(\mathcal{A})$, coincides with the upper cluster algebra $U(\Sigma)$. Inspired by the work of Shen--Sun--Weng, we introduce a localized cluster variety $\mathring{\mathcal{A}}$ whose positive real locus is the decorated Teichm\"uller space $\mathcal{T}^d(\Sigma)$. For $p\geq2$, its ring of global sections is the normalization of the classical Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ and equals that algebra except for the four-punctured sphere. In the equality cases, the quantum Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_q(\Sigma)$ provides a quantization of this global-section ring. We prove normality of $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$ for $p\geq2$, complementing its known Gorenstein property, and normality of $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$ other than $\Sigma_{0,4}$. We also prove finite generation of $U(\Sigma_{g,p})$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$, including the once-punctured case.

papers.title: Stationary diffusion on nonnegatively curved graphs
papers.abstract: Lazy random walk on a bounded-degree graph of nonnegative Ollivier–Ricci curvature has diffusive second moment and Gaussian upper tails when started in stationarity. If the maximum degree is $D$, then $\mathbb E d(X_0,X_n)^2\le4Dn$, with optimal order of dependence on $D$. The results also hold for stationary random rooted infinite graphs. The proof combines known heat-kernel total-variation decay with a reversible energy identity for the conditional mean displacement. Its exponential form controls variation between starting vertices; martingale concentration then controls the walk itself.

papers.title: Substantially Improved Rate and Distance for Addressable Transversal Phase Gates
papers.abstract: An important ingredient in fault-tolerant quantum computation is asymptotically good codes with fully addressable transversal non-Clifford gates. Existing constructions, however, provide only small explicit guarantees for rate and relative distance. Here, we substantially improve these guarantees for fully addressable transversal phase gates at every fixed level $h\ge3$ of the Clifford hierarchy, using a cyclic encoding beyond the binary CSS framework. The encoding separates logical phase control from the joint design of rate and distance, enabling two constructions with different computational costs. A deterministic polynomial-time algebraic-geometric construction gives a common asymptotic lower bound of $52/(675h)$ on both quantities. A counting argument gives an exponential-time construction with exact verification, improving this bound by a factor of approximately $2.86$. We further establish a universal upper bound for codes supporting fully addressable transversal single-qubit phase gates. Within our cyclic encoding framework, we obtain a stronger upper bound that is approximately $1.28$ times the lower bound achieved by our exponential-time construction. As concrete examples, we construct codes with $48$ and $90$ physical qubits supporting fully addressable transversal $T$ gates. These results narrow the gap between achievable code parameters and addressability bounds, providing quantitative targets for further improvements in efficient code constructions.

papers.title: Terminal Fano 4-fold Hypersurfaces via Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We construct $46{,}992$ new families of Fano $4$-fold hypersurfaces $X_d\subset\mathbb(a_1,\ldots,a_6)$ of Fano index $1$ with $d>200$, whose general members have terminal singularities. Unlike the $11{,}617$ quasismooth families classified by Brown and Kasprzyk, these are nonquasismooth, for which determining terminality can require the analysis of hyperquotient singularities. An exhaustive search has classified all nonquasismooth families with $d\leq200$, but extending this classification to higher degrees becomes computationally prohibitive. We therefore exploit the sparsity and spatial clustering of terminal examples using two best-first searches over $\mathbb{Z}^6$: one with a fixed heuristic, and the other with a neural network trained online by deep reinforcement learning. Together, the searches reach degrees up to $3{,}234$. The neural network additionally discovers an average of $79$ hard-to-reach families per run. For the most isolated examples, our conservative distance-based model gives an estimated lower bound of nearly $40\%$ of the fixed search's total step budget to discover a single such family. An ablation study demonstrates that this advantage arises from the neural network rather than stochastic exploration alone. The complete list of families is publicly available.

papers.title: The $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions of hyperelliptic curves: a generalization of Jacobi's elliptic functions and explicit solutions of a degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation
papers.abstract: The Jacobi elliptic functions $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{dn}$ and their ratios are expressed by Weierstrass's functions $\mathrm{al}_a=\sqrt{x-b_a}$ of an elliptic curve. For a hyperelliptic curve of genus $g$, Weierstrass's $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions generalize $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$ and $\mathrm{dn}$, and the modified Korteweg-de Vries and sine-Gordon equations stand behind them. In this paper we study the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions, which are defined by the sigma function shifted by the sum of two half-periods and which, together with the ratios of the $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions, generalize the remaining Jacobi elliptic functions. We determine the exact lattice of periods of $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ and show that it is single-valued on the unramified double covering of the Jacobian corresponding to the double covering $\hat{w}^2=(x-b_1)(x-b_2)$ of the curve. We show that $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ is the Wronskian of the band-edge eigenfunctions $\mathrm{al}_1$ and $\mathrm{al}_2$, so that the half-period translations realize Darboux transformations. As the main result, $\mathrm{al}_{12}$, $\mathrm{al}_2/\mathrm{al}_1$ and $1/\mathrm{al}_{12}$ satisfy one and the same degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation, whose polynomial has the double roots $0$ and $\infty$, and the half-periods act on these solutions as the M\"obius symmetries of the equation. Thus the Krichever-Novikov equation stands behind the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions. In genus one these functions reduce to $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{ns}$ and $\mathrm{dc}$.

papers.title: The 2-adic valuation of the constant for symmetric ideal Prouhet-Tarry-Escott solutions
papers.abstract: For an ideal solution of the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem of size $n$, let $C$ denote the associated constant, and let $\overline{C_n}$ be the greatest common divisor of these constants. Filaseta and Markovich obtained $v_2(\overline{C_8})\ge6$ and determined $v_2(\overline{C_9})=9$, and asked for improved lower bounds in the range $10\le n\le12$; Bera and Nair gave bounds for $n=10$ and $n=12$. We treat the symmetric case at every size, even and odd, by $2$-adic arguments throughout. A single identity, the row law, governs both parities. For $n$ even, over $\mathbb{Z}$, it splits into two regular systems and yields $v_2(C)\ge6,8,11,12,12,16,18,18$ for $n=6,8,10,\dots,20$. The values at $n=6,8,10,12$ are attained and hence exact for the symmetric constant: in the symmetric case this closes both brackets of Bera--Nair, and gives $v_2(C'_8)=8$, for which the published information was $v_2(\overline{C_8})\ge6$. We also record that the two lower bounds of Bera--Nair, $9$ at $n=10$ and $11$ at $n=12$, are attained by $2$-adic solutions symmetric about $-1/2$, so that no argument using $2$-adic information alone can raise them. For $n$ odd, over $\mathbb{Z}_2$, it combines with a finite-difference lemma refining a congruence of Filaseta--Markovich to give $v_2(C)\ge11,12,12$ for $n=11,13,15$, against $8$, $10$ and $11$ from Kleiman's bound $(n-1)!\mid C$; the chain also reproduces the known values $4,6,9$ at $n=5,7,9$. At $n=11$ the bound is sharp: the two quadratic near-solutions of Coppersmith, Mossinghoff, Scheinerman and VanderKam are symmetric ideal solutions over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ with $v_2(C)=11$, since in both of the real quadratic fields involved the prime $2$ splits. This answers, for $n=11$ and $p=2$, two questions of Filaseta--Markovich, and exhibits for those sizes the case $p\le n$ of the question closing Rees--Smyth, who construct $p$-adic ideal solutions only for $p>n$: at the prime $2$ there is no local obstruction at these sizes. At $n=13$ we exhibit a symmetric ideal solution over $\mathbb{Z}_2$, obtained from a second object of the same authors, although its constant has valuation $17$.

papers.title: The Exact One-Half Threshold for Arbitrary-Capacity Bottleneck Multiple Subset Sum
papers.abstract: In bottleneck multiple subset sum, items with weights are packed into knapsacks with capacities, possibly leaving items unpacked, so as to maximize the minimum load. For identical capacities the best possible approximation ratio is $2/3$, and Chen et al.\ asked whether $2/3$ is also achievable for arbitrary capacities. We show that it is not: for arbitrary capacities we give a $1/2$-approximation using $O(n\log(n+1)+m\log(m+1))$ arithmetic and comparison operations for $n$ items and $m$ knapsacks, and prove that no fixed ratio above $1/2$ is achievable unless $\mathsf P=\mathsf{NP}$. We also give a short proof of the classical $1/2$ guarantee of Friesen and Langston for unit profits.

papers.title: The Extension groups of one $\rm K$-type representations of graded Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We study the extension groups between one $\rm K$-type representations of the graded Hecke algebra $\mathbb H$. A one $\rm K$-type representation is a Hermitian representation of $\mbb H$ whose restriction to the Weyl group is irreducible. Using a Koszul-type resolution of $\mathbb H$-modules, we reduce the computation of $\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathbb H}^j(X,Y)$ to a combinatorial count, yielding explicit formulas for the classical types and a computer computation for the exceptional types.

papers.title: Three-machine unit-job scheduling in time O((L+2)^276)
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently gave a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for P3|prec,p_j=1|C_max (problem OPEN8 of Garey and Johnson), with running time O((L+2)^150020) on a multitape Turing machine, L being the input length; the same exponent appears in the accompanying Lean statement. The exponent comes from enumerating all Boolean formulas with at most 10000 leaves, each leaf choosing its own triple of jobs. We show that every description actually used by the structural proof involves at most 21 distinct job triples and at most 3 distinct rank thresholds. Restricting the enumerated family accordingly, and using the length bound on accepting paths already proved there to limit the number of reachability passes, the same algorithm runs in time O((L+2)^276).

papers.title: Topological Computational Paths: Presentation Invariance and Observable Quotients
papers.abstract: A computational path records the steps used to establish an equality. Topologies on computational equality witnesses can depend on the chosen generators and execution schedule, even when their algebraic and homotopical meanings agree. We study continuous presentations of finite computational paths whose declared rewrites are realized by endpoint-fixed homotopies. We compare a topology retaining the full signed trace with an observable topology recording endpoints, length, and exact path realization. Continuous finite-word interpretations that are inverse up to scoped rewriting preserve trace-sensitive quotient arrows and their final composable-pair spaces. Observable quotients behave differently. Over a point with a nonempty primitive alphabet, we classify their topology: it records length parity when all named relations preserve parity, and is otherwise indiscrete. Adjoining a conservative abbreviation can therefore turn a discrete two-element quotient into an indiscrete space, even though ordinary multiplication remains continuous. A circle presentation also gives nonhomeomorphic quotients under binary and equal-slot timing. Geometric completeness alone does not identify the trace-sensitive and observable topologies. Multiplication is continuous on the quotient of composable representatives. We characterize when this topology agrees with the ordinary pullback topology and give an open-projection criterion. Universal presentations recover classical fundamental-groupoid topology. Normal forms, primitive interchange, and a Cayley covering prove completeness for circle, torus, product, and rose presentations. A literal-word correspondence relates the semantics to the reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity fragment of equality derivations. Selected results are formalized in Lean, with the realization models and proof coverage stated explicitly.

papers.title: Torus fibrations on $3$-dimensional manifolds which are smooth functions with finitely many critical values and stable fold maps
papers.abstract: We present smooth functions which are torus fibrations with finitely many critical values on $3$-dimensional closed manifolds, from (stable) fold maps into the plane. Fold maps are higher dimensional versions of Morse functions and introduced and studied first in the 1950s by Thom and Whitney. Saeki, Sakuma, and so on, are important researchers, studying related singularity theory and differential topology mainly, since the 1990s. $3$-dimensional closed manifolds always admit ones into the plane. Surface fibrations are important tools and objects in complex geometry, symplectic geometry, and $4$-dimensional geometry. It is important to construct important examples of the fibrations. In our paper, we present a $3$-dimensional related new study. Related to this, the author has succeeded in explicit construction of explicit functions with prescribed level sets and fold maps whose singular values sets are concentric on manifolds such as connected sums of sphere bundles over spheres.

papers.title: Two examples in amplituhedron tilings
papers.abstract: We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.

papers.title: Two improved lower bounds for the 2-adic valuation of the constant of the Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.abstract: For an ideal solution of the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem of size $n$ the associated constant $C$ is divisible by a large power of $2$. Restricting to symmetric solutions, we prove two new lower bounds for $v_2(C)$: $v_2(C)\ge14$ at $n=15$, improving $12$, and $v_2(C)\ge19$ at $n=20$, improving $18$; both earlier bounds are those of the companion article hexagon:2611.00057. The first rests on two identities satisfied by every symmetric solution of odd size, one relating $v_2(C)$ to a difference of two products and one turning the index relation into an equality, together with an arithmetic criterion for a block of entries of equal valuation. The second rests on an identity internal to each of the two sides, from which we deduce that the vanishing of the cross invariant $R$ forces $k_0\equiv0\pmod4$ when $k_0\ge4$. Two self-contained verifiers accompany the note.

papers.title: Ulam Metric \(k\)-Center in Parameterized Linear Time
papers.abstract: Continuous Ulam Metric \(k\)-Center asks for at most \(k\) permutations whose radius-\(d\) balls cover the input rankings. For \(m\) rankings of \(n\) symbols, a deterministic algorithm takes \(2^{O(kd\log(k+d+2))}mn\) word operations. Permanent reference rankings, short insertion lists, and small obstructions obtained by patience sorting control the search. For one center, this answers a question of Bai, Fomin, Golovach, More, and Wietheger with linear input dependence. An arbitrary-alphabet Hamming embedding with a nonexpansive retraction also gives the matching \(2^{o(d\log d)}\) exclusion under the Exponential Time Hypothesis.

papers.title: Universal Formulas for de Jonqui\`eres Loci and Equivariant Contact Problems
papers.abstract: Given a family of genus $g$ curves $f:\Psi\to S$ and a relative degree $d$ line bundle $L$ on $\Psi$ such that $f_*L$ is a vector bundle, the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ is stratified by relative de Jonqui\`eres loci, which parameterize sections of $L$ with prescribed vanishing orders. We give universal formulas for the classes of these loci in terms of the relative $O(1)$ on $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ and tautological classes pulled back from the universal Picard stack $\mathrm{Pic}_g^d$. When $f$ is the family of lines in $\mathbb{P}^r$, we use the universal polynomials to compute $\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}$-equivariant classes of loci of hypersurfaces and complete intersections admitting lines with prescribed contact orders.

papers.title: Universal-Clique Amplification and Hardness of Assignment-Optimal Edge Clique Covers
papers.abstract: An edge clique cover has assignment cost equal to the sum of its clique sizes. Unless $P=NP$, this cost admits no polynomial-time $O(N^{1/2-\eta})$-approximation for any fixed $0<\eta<1/2$, even on connected $N$-vertex graphs. A universal-clique join transfers coloring hardness without the additive obstruction in earlier reductions. Its exact residual formula also exhibits a change of optimal cover when a universal twin is added. Explicit counterexamples refute two proposed twin-extension rules, while weighted compression of true-twin classes preserves the optimum.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the Strassen CP Rank Gap and Symmetric Rank Gap of Third-Order Tensors
papers.abstract: For two third-order tensors over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, we define the Strassen CP rank gap as the sum of their CP ranks minus the CP rank of their direct sum. For arbitrary third-order tensors, we derive explicit upper bounds on this gap in terms of CP rank excess and dimension. For symmetric third-order tensors, we similarly define the Strassen symmetric rank gap using symmetric rank and establish explicit upper bounds in terms of symmetric rank excess, CP rank excess, and dimension. These bounds also yield sufficient conditions for the respective gaps to vanish, ensuring additivity of CP rank or symmetric rank under direct sums.

papers.title: Witt groups of smooth real curves and surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the $\mathbf{I}^*$-cohomology of a smooth real algebraic curve in terms of its real locus and its geometric genus. We notably extend results of Knebusch and Monnier to the twisted case. We further describe how to compute twisted Witt groups of surfaces, generalising work of Sujatha, and apply our results to the computation of the shifted and twisted Witt groups of the smooth real anisotropic quadric surface. Finally, we extend Monnier's investigation of the image of the global signature homomorphism for surfaces.
